messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1941504321 - Elevated CUDA OOMs and node flaps observed in runtime-pool-3. Alerting from autoscaler + crashloop detector. Severity: P1.

sam: looking. seeing steady increase in OOMs over last ~4h, a few nodes went Unhealthy and were recycled. No single big spike — more like slow memory drift.

carla: logs from one of the crashed containers show repeated `cudaMalloc` failures followed by the runtime OOM handler killing the process. stack traces point at kvcache allocator during attention paging.

carla: snippet from /var/log/redwood/runtime/last.log:```
[2026-11-04T09:12:03Z] ERR cuda: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-11-04T09:12:03Z] WRN kvcache: slab_fragmentation: free_slots=512 used_slots=131000 total_slots=131512
[2026-11-04T09:12:03Z] ERR allocator: paged-alloc request failed -> OOM
```

lee: looks classic: fragmentation + slow leak in paged attention path. We've had similar patterns but this one is more gradual — likely cross-request KV growth + imperfect eviction.

sam: impact: about 12% of requests to hosted region-us-east-1 are seeing increased latency/retries, 3% error rate spike. Some dedicated customers on pool-3 saw degraded throughput. Zhen, can you confirm which customers were routed to pool-3 in the last 6h?

zhen: pulling lists now. (ETA 5m)

ben_platform: adding runbooks: we should avoid full cluster reboot. Prefer targeted mitigation: reduce per-model KV retention window, bump eviction aggressiveness, and enable temporary routing to warm fallback models.

sam: plan: 1) scale down batch size and reduce prefix cache retention to force more evictions; 2) adjust runtime config on pool-3 nodes: kv_evict_threshold -> 0.65 from 0.8; 3) cordon the worst 3 nodes and drain in rotation; 4) enable fallbacks for heavy customers to smaller model variant. Agree?

carla: yes. quick command to set runtime flag via admin API:```bash
curl -X POST https://console.internal.redwood/api/v1/pools/pool-3/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"kv_evict_threshold":0.65, "kv_retention_secs":600}'
```

sam: applying now to one node as canary.

incident-bot: Deploy started: patch-config pool-3 node-12 by sam at 2026-11-04T09:25:10Z.

carla: canary looks good so far. metrics: node-12 mem-Used trend reversed within ~3 min. eviction count jumped x3 which is expected. No new OOMs on node-12 since change.

lee: start rolling to remaining nodes but do 2 nodes at a time with 10m observation windows. Keep autoscale enabled.

sam: rolling update initiated. Also opened temporary routing rule to divert >=80% traffic from pool-3 to pool-2 for non-enterprise keys:```json
{
  "match": {"customer_tier":"standard"},
  "route_to": "pool-2",
  "duration_secs": 7200
}
```

zhen: customer impact: affected dedicated customers A and C on pool-3 experienced higher retries; we've notified both and offered to migrate to pool-2 temporarily. Enterprise B is on a separate dedicated cluster, unaffected.

carla: discovered subtle bug in eviction accounting: small empty slots weren't being coalesced after paged dealloc which means fragmentation slowly increases. We'll draft a hotfix but it's not safe to roll globally mid-incident.

ben_platform: action items: (1) keep eviction threshold lowered for 2hrs, (2) continue gradual roll of config across pool-3, (3) start immediate patch branch for allocator defrag algorithm, target PR by EOD, (4) post-incident QA with reproducer.

sam: monitoring: latency back to normal for pool-12s routing shift. Error rate trending down from 3% -> 0.7% after first 30m. Node flaps reduced.

incident-bot: NOTE: incident annotated in pagerduty: PD-7891. Handoff required? oncall shift ends in 40m.

lee: I'll take handoff. summary pinned above + runbook steps executed. Next steps for next oncall: finish roll, push allocator defrag PR, coordinate post-mortem and customer follow-ups.

zhen: confirmed both A and C accepted temporary migration to pool-2, ETA migrations complete 12m.

sam: quick diagnostic commands we ran (for runbook):```bash
# observe fragmentation stats
redwood-admin metrics get --pool pool-3 --metric kvcache.fragmentation
# toggle evict threshold
redwood-admin config set --pool pool-3 kv_evict_threshold=0.65
# drain node
kubectl cordon node/node-12
kubectl drain node/node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

carla: leaving note: we should add an automated guard that lowers kv_evict_threshold when per-node eviction-rate drops below X but free memory is decreasing. Prevents human-in-loop next time.

lee: agreed. will add to backlog and prioritize after hotfix.

sam: status at 09:50Z: rolling update 8/10 nodes done, no new OOMs reported, error rate back to baseline for standard traffic.

incident-bot: RESOLVED? marking as mitigated. Please confirm.

lee: mitigated. moving to monitoring state. I'll own postmortem. tagging #postmortems.

carla: creating follow-up ticket TRACK-512: "kvcache defrag hotfix + adaptive eviction guard" with reproducer and perf tests.

zhen: customer messages sent. support to follow up with logs and root-cause note tomorrow.

sam: thanks all. final note: do not revert kv_evict_threshold until allocator defrag PR lands and is validated.

ben_platform: thanks team — great coordination. :)
